# Revision log — OWNED editorial revision of 14 September 2026

This log records how each recommendation in `REVIEW.md` (the collection review) and the per-post `REVIEW.md` files was handled. The review files are unchanged and remain the baseline. "Implemented" means the recommendation was applied as written; "Adapted" means the intent was met a different way; "Declined" means it was not applied, with the reason; "Unresolved" means work or verification that could not be completed in this pass.

## Collection-level decisions

**Structure (collection review §"Reading order, combinations and worthwhile additions")**

- Split the handover material out of "The Roadmap Did Not Slip, the Financing Did" → **Implemented.** New Part V chapter `25-handover-of-obligations` ("Hand Over the Obligations, Not Just the Company", permalink `handover-of-obligations`). Chapter 18 keeps its permalink and title and is now a focused delayed-financing chapter with a completed, dated funding decision.
- Move "Fix the Decision Problem Before Adding People" directly after "Can the Software and the Team Deliver What Was Promised?" → **Implemented** in `config.yaml`; Part III introduction groups the nine chapters into three moves; handoffs rewritten (09→13→27→10).
- Optional fund-economics reference for waterfalls and fund ratios → **Implemented.** New reference page `fund-economics` ("Fund Economics: Fees, Distributions and Performance Reports") receives the €160 waterfall from chapter 2 and DPI/RVPI/TVPI material from chapter 4; both chapters link to it as optional depth.
- Combine "Find the Help" and "Useful Engagement" for a shorter edition → **Declined.** Kept separate with sharpened jobs (sourcing decision vs filled charter and scope change); repeated provider/charter advice removed instead.
- Keep Hilton/Skype paired; keep Visma and TeamSystem separate; keep acquisition and separation in one chapter with visible substructure → **Implemented.**
- Add a documented venture funding delay / minority case and a corporate ownership case → **Declined for this pass.** No documented case with adequate evidence was available without inventing facts; the evidence-scope disclosure is preserved in the guide, Part VI introduction and bibliography. Recorded as an open item.
- Companion evidence essay for healthcare/research methods → **Declined.** The finale keeps the material findings and shortens the methodological exposition instead.
- Three short reading routes in the guide → **Implemented** (plus the previous situation routes, consolidated into one table).
- Complete finding-to-funded-plan-to-review example → **Implemented** as a shared fictional chain (finding D-3, initiative ONB-1) through chapters 22–25 (diligence, first hundred days, financing slipped, handover) and the toolkit; figures and assumptions are stated in each chapter and labelled fictional.

**Titles (collection review §3)** — permalinks and ids unchanged: "Match the Funding to the Work" (raise-what-you-need); "Find the Cash Behind Your Technology Budget" (obligations-before-budget); "Toys R Us: Positive Operating Earnings, Too Little Cash" (toys-r-us); "TeamSystem: Each New Owner Inherits Progress and Unfinished Work" (teamsystem). Visma's title decision is recorded in its entry.

**Terminology (collection review §"Voice, readability and terminology")** — a terminology sheet (investor/firm/fund/company; shareholder vs accountable leader; financial sponsor vs investor-side sponsor vs company sponsor; funding states from expression of interest to cash received; named profit measures; financial vs causal contribution; end-to-end work lead time vs DORA change lead time; continuing service as a legitimate outcome; thesis and durable value) governed every chapter revision and the glossary.

**Categorical ownership contrasts (collection review §1)** — the "companies without investors do X; under investors Y" pattern was removed from every opening, summary and comic introduction listed in the review and replaced by the conditional pattern ("this arrangement changes the conditions of the decision; establish the actual funding, authority and deadline before committing", then the specific condition).

**Companion formats** — summaries were rewritten to carry the revised argument and checked against a 300–500-word prose convention (front matter absent; figure lines and `[S..]` citation tokens excluded). Comic text (introductions, captions, dialogue, JSON prompt/alt/caption fields) was edited; no panel images could be regenerated in this pass (no image-generation key available). Panels whose new text the existing image cannot fully carry are flagged `needs_regeneration` in their JSON and listed per post below.

**Not changed** — `REVIEW.md` files; permalinks; ids; image files; `_research/` provenance (except a new `bibliography-revision-history.md` receiving the editorial chronology moved out of the public bibliography).

# Revision log — OWNED editorial revision of 15 September 2026

This pass implements the reassessed reviews dated 14–15 September 2026 (collection `REVIEW.md` and the 41 per-post `REVIEW.md` files, which are unchanged and remain the independent baseline). It was coordinated as one pass with one agent per post, run in dependency order: standalone chapters first, then the shared-scenario clusters after a canonical record was fixed, then the reading guide, Part V introduction, toolkit and bibliography. Every per-post entry below is the agent's own report of what changed, what was adapted or declined, what stays unresolved and what was verified; the coordinator checked cross-links, summary lengths, comic metadata, the build and the shared figures across posts.

## Collection-level decisions

- **One canonical shared-scenario record.** Two read-only inventories of every passage carrying the shared Larkspur examples showed the chain could not be reconciled sentence by sentence, so the coordinator fixed one dated ledger before any of those chapters was edited. It is kept in `_journals/private-techuity/_research/shared-scenario-record.md` (outside the site build). The decisions that changed text: the first-hundred-days envelope is **€500,000 and 24 engineer-weeks** (the allocation chapter's figure), so the allocation, early-plan, recovery, toolkit and handover chapters now describe one plan; KNW-1 is four protected specialist-weeks outside the 24; portal research (€20,000 / 2 weeks) is a funded plan line; the REC-1 correction and retest cost **€20,000 / 2 weeks from the reserve, approved by the board around day 47**; the day-100 data-quality step uses the last four weeks and €40,000, leaving **€160,000 and no uncommitted weeks**; ONB-1 is **€180,000 committed, about €90,000 incurred by day 100, €90,000 payable over the next two quarters**, with €30,000/yr maintenance from the operating budget from the next financial year; the day-20 baseline is reconstructed from the twelve implementations of the previous two quarters; Priya measures the cohort at day 90 and the board decides at day 100 under one pre-set rule (**< 60 h green, 60–70 h amber, > 70 h or no reduction red**; 62 h is amber); gate 2 at month six is ≤ 50 h with waiting time down; the expansion decision moves to the next quarterly review (≈ day 190) and expansion is not before month 13; the delegation rule is that Ines authorizes spending inside the approved plan while reserve draws, changes to what the envelope funds and hires outside the headcount plan are the board's.
- **Pilot cost basis and the funding-choice loan.** €75/h fully loaded, 2,000 hours per FTE-year, so an implementation specialist costs €150,000 a year and two cost €300,000; the pilot is €180,000 build plus €30,000/yr maintenance everywhere (the obligations chapter's €200,000 aligned); released staff time is capacity until a dated conversion is evidenced. The funding-choice loan is a **four-year** €750,000 term loan at 8% with a one-year principal holiday (payments €60,000 / €310,000 / €290,000 / €270,000, closing at zero) tested against €350,000 of operating cash alone.
- **Finale cost split.** The €220,000 is €150,000 of specialist payroll (cash, ending only when protected customer contracts allow) plus €70,000 of released support time (capacity); Option A as written is inadmissible under the scenario's own contract rule; Option B saves €80,000 of cash from year two after ≈€75,000 of one-off specialist retention.
- **The financing-delay chapter is a separate scenario.** It keeps its own cash, burn, hires and dates, no longer uses the shared identifiers or ledger figures, and says so; the reading guide, Part V introduction, handover chapter and toolkit describe the chain as diligence → early plan → handover, with earlier pilot and support episodes in Parts III–IV.
- **Investor callouts.** Kept where they name a financing or governance consequence, shortened or reworded where they restated the learning outcome or reintroduced a universal claim; "the investor reports to its investors" became a fund manager reporting to its fund's investors where that is the actor.
- **Confirmed factual corrections.** Unicorn study: reported valuations average about 50% above modelled fair value (NBER version; the published JFE version says 48%). Fund catch-up: a slower catch-up changes timing, not necessarily the final split. TeamSystem: the €72.0m net finance charge is an accounting figure; €52.1m of finance costs were paid (Note 10), and the 2024 £34.189m gross realization proceeds are reported separately from the £24.3m July announcement, neither a net distribution. Hilton's OnQ is dated to 2003/2005 pre-buyout filings; Skype's Qik acquisition and group video calling to January 2011 (S-1/A).

**Files changed:** index.md, summary.md, comics.md, spec.md, `assets/images/01-announcement-is-not-a-budget/four-separate-organizations.jpeg` (regenerated), `assets/images/01-announcement-is-not-a-budget/capital-commitment-to-company-cash.jpeg` (regenerated), `_research/article-illustration-prompts-20260913.json` (both entries re-keyed to the current slug, with the previous prompt and checksum retained), `docs/private-techuity/announcement-is-not-a-budget.html`, `.spec.html` and the two built copies of the figures.
**Implemented:**

"Only the primary part … increases the company's cash" and the summary's "only money paid for newly issued shares reaches the company" are gone. - AIB-002 (medium) — terminology → defined at first use in the article: budget, valuation, share/shareholder, transaction costs, closing, transaction, prepayment (recap), minority funding round, buyout, corporate group, onboarding engineers, €8 million (€8m), venture and growth investors, entity, fund (a pool of investors' money managed under agreed rules; "investment vehicle" and "committed capital" removed), proceeds, financial sponsor, limited partners, capital call, equity, distribution (all before the diagram), lenders' contractual protections, "has already placed all the money it may invest" (for fully invested), €2 billion, debt, balance sheet (owns / owes / left for owners), cloud migration, pension funds and insurers, capital, partnership and limited partnership agreement, private funds, private-equity fund, exit, management fee (with its calculation base), carried interest "also called carry", investment profits, "the detailed rules for sharing investment proceeds … the distribution waterfall", realization in words, shared-cost splitting and services from connected organizations, the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) expanded, subscription agreement, issuer in words, chief executive officer (CEO), closing statement, shareholders' agreement, board minutes, reserved matters, investor director, runway, net spending, cash plan, onboarding volume, "cash it expects to generate from running the business", "an investor with plenty of money and a company short of cash", purchase price (for transaction consideration), "interest and repayment instalments" (for service it), public corporation and patient capital in the reading list. Preferred return, catch-up and clawback are no longer named in the chapter (they stay in [[fund-economics]]). # Revision log — in-depth review of Match the Funding to the Work, 17 September 2026

Response to round 1 of the in-depth review (`.in-depth-reviews/20260917-172341.VpdY3Z/round-01.review.md`, findings RWN-001 to RWN-009 plus the terminology audit). The spec (success criteria, `revised:` and changelog) was updated before the article; permalink, id and title unchanged; the loan schedule, the €610,000 need and every previously published number are unchanged.

## 04-raise-what-you-need — Match the Funding to the Work (`raise-what-you-need`)

**Files changed:** spec.md, index.md, summary.md, comics.md, the regenerated panel image `comic-06-scene.jpeg` (via `_research/generate_comics.py`, shared cast reference; the superseded panel archived by the generator under `_research/discarded-comic-variants/04-raise-what-you-need-comic-06-scene-54dbcb3f2a17.jpeg`) and the regenerated article figure `one-product-different-funding-plans.jpeg` (via the article-illustrator script from a staged placeholder, `--overwrite --replace`), the generator records `_research/comic-generation-prompts-20260913.json` and `comic-generation-progress-20260913.json` (updated by the generator, with the panel’s previous prompt kept), the figure record `_research/article-illustration-prompts-20260913.json` (new prompt, alt, caption and sha256 for this figure with the previous prompt and hash kept), this log, and the rebuilt `docs/private-techuity/raise-what-you-need.html`, `raise-what-you-need.spec.html` and the two copied images. Panels 1–5, Figure 2, the summary overview, logo and icon are unchanged as files.

- RWN-001 (high) — annual-flow shortfall confused with inability to pay; year-one €290,000 unexplained; reserve arithmetic contradicted → **Implemented.** New stated assumptions: Larkspur holds €250,000, the board’s minimum balance is €200,000, so €50,000 is unrestricted. New “Cash balance, base case and downside” table (cash above the minimum, years 1–4): opening €50,000; loan €750,000; operating cash €350,000 a year; work paid for €420,000 in year one (build, transition, twelve months of the contract specialist) and €30,000 in year two (first maintenance year, the financial year after the step ships); payments €60,000 / €310,000 / €290,000 / €270,000; closing €670,000 / €680,000 / €740,000 / €820,000; still held for the work €330,000 / €300,000 (unspent allowance and runway, maintenance still to pay, the €140,000 reserve; released after the eighteen funded months); downside closing €670,000 / €630,000 / €640,000 / €670,000. The year-one margin is retained cash and is what covers the downside. The €10,000 is now described as a year-two operating-cash deficit covered from retained cash, not a missed payment; on the forecast no payment is missed in either case, and the text says what would make one missed. Consuming the cushion is distinguished from underfunding the work: using €10,000 of the reserve for a payment leaves the €610,000 funded and the cushion at €130,000 (the former “short by the same amount” sentence removed). Maintenance after the funded period stated as an ordinary operating cost inside the €350,000 forecast from year three. The front-loading paragraph now reconciles with the same figures (€345,000 of spending against about €175,000 of operating cash in the first two quarters and €50,000 unrestricted: about €120,000 below the required balance by month six). Sam’s strict test (each year’s payment from that year’s operating cash alone) is kept and labelled as the conservative rule; the “Revisit” section now says the year-two margin has retained year-one cash and the reserve behind it.
- RWN-002 (medium) — amber fallback needs four engineer-weeks the money-only reserve cannot supply → **Implemented.** New paragraph “Who does the work, and when”: the twelve engineer-weeks are three engineers for four weeks (step usable from about day 35; the implementation team sets up the eight cohort customers between day 35 and day 90); the €40,000 comes from the reserve and buys a data-validation service plus the contract specialist’s time correcting customer records; the four engineer-weeks are two of the same three engineers for two weeks from day 100, which moves the reporting improvements they were due to start back by two weeks; the step is ready by about month four, the second cohort of eight is set up in months four to six and measured at month six; the internal and contract specialists stay on the transition and the cohorts are set up by the implementation team, so no one is booked twice. The need table and the scarce-capacity paragraph now say engineer-weeks are effort, not elapsed time. The amber rule no longer says the engineer-weeks come “from the €140,000 reserve”.
- RWN-003 (medium) — assumed finance vocabulary → **Implemented** in all three formats. Article: raise and round (WHY INVESTORS CARE), rescue round, dilute returns (“spreading the same gain over more money invested”), runway, shares, valuation and returns, migration, investor type as “money in exchange for a share of ownership”, financing as borrowed versus exchanged for ownership, acquisition; the arrangement table gained a “What it is” column with one-phrase explanations of venture, growth, buyout, corporate minority, corporate acquisition and continued founder ownership (reinvestment, integration and concentration of risk reworded in plain words); operating cash, equity, growth equity, minority stake, approval rights, term loan, principal, interest, principal holiday, loan balance (table headings relabelled “Loan balance at start/end”, “Principal repaid”), contribution and “collected”, collections and renewals, data-quality step, cohort (eight customers, measured ninety days after the board adopts the plan), shareholders’ agreement, acquisition borrowing, worked bridge, majority and minority investor, private equity, EBITDA (expanded and “not money in the bank”), working capital; seed investor, exits, the four contract rights and bootstrap finance glossed in the reading list. Ines, Sam and Alex are introduced by plain role (chief executive, runs finances, leads engineering); the CEO/CFO/CTO abbreviations no longer appear in the three reader-facing files. Summary and comic: see RWN-005 and RWN-006.
- RWN-004 (medium) — 306-word decision paragraph; data-quality step and month six referenced before the decision that triggers them → **Implemented.** The paragraph is now seven short ones in this order: The choice (recommendation and the strict test, focusing on year two) → The dated review (day 90 / day 100, thresholds) → Who does the work, and when → Cash balance, base case and downside (table plus the downside paragraph) → Why the €135,000 is left out (the three dated mechanisms) → What the reserve is for → the rejected alternatives → What would reverse the decision. The four margins are no longer repeated in prose after the table.
- RWN-005 (medium) — summary’s thresholds lack unit, baseline and sample; “day-90 cohort, decided at day 100”; cash qualification dropped → **Implemented.** New paragraph “The decision is dated”: at day 90 Priya measures the first eight customers set up with the new step, in staff hours per customer, from 80 today with 50 the target; the board decides at day 100; the three bands follow. Operating cash restored as “about €350,000 a year after tax and existing obligations, before interest on new borrowing”. - DB-011 (medium) — the €800,000 carry needed a stated distribution-stage assumption → **Fixed.** Step 4 of the payout arithmetic now states the assumption (every payment the fund agreement puts ahead of the manager has already been made, so each further euro of profit splits 80% to the fund’s investors and 20% to the manager) and shows 20% × €3.99 million = €798,000, about €800,000, with about €3.2 million to the fund’s investors. The following paragraph says a 20% rate does not by itself mean 20% of the next €4 million: a fund can be in profit and still short of the point where investors have their money and any preferred return back, in which case this money pays no carry; just past it a catch-up can give the manager more than 20% for a while; [[fund-economics]] works the stages. The four-bets table cell now reads “only once the fund has paid its investors everything its agreement puts first”. The summary keeps the amount with the same condition (“if the fund has already paid its investors everything its agreement puts first, so further profit splits 80/20. A profitable fund short of that point pays none yet”) and says the €100 million threshold has been passed.

The board authorizes a pause contingency of up to €30,000 beside the €550,000 (most authorized: €580,000), and the finance leader runs the dated cash check on the longest authorized pause as well (three more months of payroll and premises, plus the €30,000). A new item separates continued payroll and premises (not new spending; the pause postpones €25,000 of saving a month) from the extra retention payments (new spending, from the contingency). “What goes back to the board”: a pause over three months, dropping a stage, new spending beyond €580,000, or a cash position in which the pause case can no longer be confirmed. “If a specialist leaves anyway”: the payment cannot require anyone to stay; the main-team engineer walked through that specialist’s customers takes them over with the other specialists’ help, the board is told, and paid cover beyond the approved amounts needs its approval. The three-month stage-two pause is worked through: gate passed at the end of month thirteen, the five leave and the location closes at month fifteen, full saving from month sixteen, €75,000 of saving postponed and €30,000 of retention payments added.

- PT11-001 (medium) — EBITDA, expensed and capitalized unexplained → **Fixed.** The article defines earnings as profit and lists the four items EBITDA leaves out in ordinary words: interest as the cost of borrowing; taxes on the company’s profit, distinguished from the sales taxes on customer invoices; depreciation for physical assets; amortization for assets such as software. It says what remains is roughly sales minus day-to-day running costs, and does not equate EBITDA with operating income. A new paragraph explains expensing and capitalizing, why a capitalized replacement can leave EBITDA looking healthy while it consumes cash, and that the money has left the bank either way. The summary has its own shorter explanation and the cash caveat.
- PT11-002 (medium) — opening terms, roles, comic boilerplate → **Fixed.** “Binding constraint” is introduced as “the obstacle that most limits the plan” in the excerpt, callouts and key points. WHY INVESTORS CARE now explains the investment case and replaces “reprice or resequence” with reconsidering the price the investor is willing to pay, or agreeing a different order and timing of work. Dependencies and the board are explained at first use. Alex is introduced as Larkspur’s technology leader and Sam as its finance leader. The Larkspur example was already the first paragraph; the two framing paragraphs after it were merged and shortened. The comic introduction now sets up Larkspur and the cast and drops the sentences about fund scenarios and historical cases, which this comic never uses.
- PT11-003 (medium) — lead-time comparison inaccessible → **Fixed.** A commit is explained as recording a code change in the team’s shared version history; production is defined at its first use as the live system customers use. DORA is expanded as DevOps Research and Assessment and metric gaming is explained. The 169-word paragraph is now three: the two clocks and their start and end points, Larkspur’s two readings, and what the gap does not prove. The “requested or started” wording now says this book starts the end-to-end clock at the request. The summary explains the commit in words, expands DORA, and drops the SPACE acronym from its prose while keeping the S13 citation beside the claim it supports. The article keeps SPACE’s five dimensions. Five metrics and commit-to-production are unchanged.
- PT11-004 (medium) — abstract option terms → **Fixed.** The module definition moved to its first use. Configuration is defined as changing settings rather than writing new code. “Contracts” reading the rules became “the tool that generates customer contracts”, in the prose and in the finding’s Current evidence row. The bounded interface is explained with the concrete case: a handful of trial customers invoiced under their own rules, kept separate, while the existing billing system runs unchanged for everyone else. The company-owned boundary is explained in the finding table; “repeatable capability” became a setup Larkspur can reuse for many customers and further countries. Onboarding, incidents, integration layer, parallel running, migration, exception handling, financing, parent company, cloud provider and release toolchain are explained at first use; “diligence report”, “material item”, “exit rights”, “enterprise platform” and “economically negative” were replaced with plain wording. # Revision log — in-depth review, round 1, of Clarify AI Strategy: Three Different Investment Questions, 22 September 2026

All eleven findings (`round-01.review.md`, AI16-001 to AI16-011) were checked against the current files and the actual images; all were supported. The spec was updated first (six criteria added, `revised: 2026-09-22`, changelog line). Permalink, `id`, title, author and date unchanged. No study figure, citation or source claim changed; the fictional scenario's existing budgets, dates and decisions were preserved, and the new figures added are derived from them.

**Files changed:** spec.md (first), index.md, summary.md, comics.md, four regenerated images (`three-ai-investment-questions.jpeg`, `summary-at-a-glance.jpeg`, `comic-01-scene.jpeg`, `comic-04-scene.jpeg`), this log, the rebuilt `docs/private-techuity/ai-strategy-three-questions.html` and `.spec.html` with their copied assets, and `manuscripts/owned/ai-strategy-three-questions.md` with the export manifest. Figure 2 (`measure-the-whole-ai-workflow.jpeg`), the logo, the icon and comic panels 2, 3, 5 and 6 are unchanged: no finding concerns their artwork, and panels 3 and 6 needed caption text only.

- AI16-001 (high) — hiring fallback required recruiting retrospectively → **Fixed.** The support example gains a "hiring dates and what each outcome costs" block: recruitment takes about three months; a failed 29 January check opens the role at once and still reaches roughly 1 April 2027, avoiding nothing; a passed check opens the role on 1 July 2027 for the 1 October start; a volume breach after the deferral cannot restore April, so a March breach gives a 1 July start and avoids three months (€16,000), not six, and the months already avoided are not erased. Interim cover is funded rather than assumed: €9,000 held by Sam for up to three months of agency support, released by the operations lead on the month a breach is confirmed. A warning short of a breach opens the role contingently. The table and summary carry the same rule.
- AI16-002 (medium) — cash mixed with existing staff time; rollout wrongly grouped with recurring costs → **Fixed.** €64,000 is stated as salary plus employer taxes, benefits and equipment, money actually paid out. The €6,000 pilot is stated as all cash. €32,000 is called employment cost avoided; the deductions are split into €3,600 licenses and €4,400 evaluation upkeep (cash, recurring) and €2,000 rollout and training (one week of the operations lead's existing time, one-time), so **€22,000 is labelled a cost-based estimate**, of which about €24,000 is cash not paid out and €2,000 is internal time. From 2028 the running cost is about €8,000 a year. ## 23 September 2026 — in-depth review of `32-handover-of-obligations` (round 2, findings HND-003, HND-008, HND-011, HND-012)

The spec was updated first: the plain-language criterion now requires proceeds to be kept apart from realized return (with the €100 → €120 example) and from the estimated value of stakes still held, and requires standalone formats to define shares; the day-190 criterion now requires the day-130 acceptance and the conditional review in every format, including the final comic caption. - **HND-011** (medium): realized return equated with money received → **Fixed.** The article now keeps three figures apart: **proceeds** (money actually received from a sale), the **realized return** (the gain or loss on what was sold: proceeds against the money originally invested, after fees and other costs, allowing for when money went in and came out) and the estimated value of any stake still held. Worked example: €100 invested and €120 received is €120 of proceeds and a €20 gain before fees and taxes; the same €20 is a better result in one year than in five. "The money invested" was added to the list of things to follow, and **cash flows** is glossed as every dated payment in and out. Wording checked against Investor.gov's glossary ("the profit or loss on an investment" over a period). The long paragraph was split in two.
